leads.summary: The current quattro tip conflicts with the Wallclock qmldir registration
leads.consequence: The PR cannot currently merge automatically (GitHub reports CONFLICTING). The base tip added IpcRegistry and ShellIpc after the PR's pinned base, and git merge-file reports a conflict between `singleton Wallclock 1.0 Wallclock.qml` and `ShellIpc 1.0 ShellIpc.qml`. Taking only Wallclock loses the ShellIpc type used by the current base's clock widget and shell; retain all three registrations when rebasing. With both conflicting lines retained, a staged current-base merged clock test passes 175 checks.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus; coordinator verified mergeable_state dirty; published (More findings)

leads.summary: Three other open wake-refresh PRs would still reset an open calendar if combined with this PR
leads.consequence: This PR's onJumped handler only resyncs the clock, preserving a calendar left on another month; it does not intercept omarchy.clock refresh. #12277 calls root.refresh() on resume; #9509 and #13658 add `omarchy-shell -q omarchy.clock refresh` on wake or sleep-monitor restart. The widget broadcasts refresh to every live clock widget, and widget refresh calls the loaded panel's refresh(), which unconditionally calls goToToday(). Thus when an open calendar is browsing another month and either refresh path runs, its month resets even after this PR merges. Coordinate/remodel refresh before combining them; they are open, diverged (not stacked) and the other PRs are GitHub MERGEABLE at inspection time.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F2; published as still present (source-level)

leads.summary: Clock test accepts a watchdog that never emits its jumped signal
leads.consequence: A plausible regression keeps the tested discontinuity predicate but makes its true branch empty. Both widget Connections remain present yet cannot receive a signal; the entire 175-check test still passes, so the wiring assertions do not guarantee wall-clock jumps are reported. Assert the live `root.jumped(elapsed)` call with the predicate, or exercise the signal in a QML test.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus N3; published in optional note

leads.summary: Clock test accepts an uninitialized first-tick wall-clock baseline
leads.consequence: Replacing `lastTick: Date.now()` with `lastTick: 0` passes all 175 checks because the assertions only cover updating the baseline later. The first tick then spuriously declares a huge forward step even when time never moved. Add an initial baseline assertion or exercise the first two watchdog ticks.
leads.triage: dropped: low value (one harmless extra resync at startup); not sent for follow-up

leads.summary: A fourth open PR may race the watchdog and refresh a browsing calendar on resume
leads.consequence: #13541 adds a five-second stale-minute check whose true branch invokes root.refresh(), which also refreshes an open panel and calls goToToday(). If its overdue callback fires before this PR's 1-second watchdog after a suspend, the panel may jump to today. The two PRs are diverged; neither merged-timer ordering nor a live wake was run. Confirm ordering with a deterministic QML fixture before treating this as a guaranteed race; the unconditional H2 paths are independently confirmed.
leads.triage: hypothesis; merged into F2 as source-level path, which Opus independently traced

The PR body still calls this "a plausible fix", so readers may expect it to fix that issue. **Suggested change:** Drop the #13275 reference and link #7608 and #13504, which match this PR's symptom.
Details The reporter's reply: https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/issues/13275#issuecomment-5857491666 (`date` printed `Sat Sep 26 10:25:02 AM PDT 2026` when `Sun Sep 27 08:50:00 AM PDT 2026` was expected). This is read from the issue, not reproduced. **Related PRs.** All four are open and reach `Panel.refresh()` → `goToToday()`, which moves a calendar left open on another month back to today (source-level, not run): ``` #12277: SystemSleep.resumed -> BarWidget.refresh() -> Panel.refresh() -> goToToday() #9509: omarchy-system-wake -> omarchy.clock refresh -> BarWidget.refresh() -> Panel.refresh() #13541: 5 s stale-minute Timer -> BarWidget.refresh() -> Panel.refresh() #13658: omarchy-system-sleep-monitor -> omarchy.clock refresh -> BarWidget.refresh() -> Panel.refresh() ``` The reconciliation in the author reply (the other paths calling `Wallclock.resync()` instead of `Panel.refresh()` while the panel is open) would avoid this. #10138 is also still open. **Verified:** - `clock-test.sh` passes at the head (175 ok) and after merging into the pinned base `c5b4db7` (175 ok). - Each of the 7 mutants in the author's table, plus removal of the early return, fails a new assertion at the head; the 7 survive at `51d4279`. - In headless Quickshell 0.3.1, `resync()` leaves a clock bound to `false` disabled and bound; at `51d4279` it started that clock and dropped the binding. A clock bound to `true` is still re-read and still loses its binding, as the new docs say. - A disabled `SystemClock` re-reads the wall clock when it is enabled again. - The docs snippet now imports `Quickshell`.
Reproducer: resync and a bound enabled Headless Quickshell 0.3.1 (Qt 6.11.2), offscreen platform, no compositor. Run from the root of a checkout; it copies that checkout's `shell/Commons` (with the PR's `Wallclock.qml`, `WallclockMath.js` and `qmldir`) unchanged into a temporary config. ```bash #!/bin/bash # Run from the root of an omarchy checkout. Needs quickshell (0.3.1 here); no # compositor: the platform is offscreen and nothing opens a window. set -u dir=$(mktemp -d) cp -r shell/Commons "$dir/Commons" cat > "$dir/shell.qml" <<'QML' import QtQuick import Quickshell import qs.Commons ShellRoot { id: root property bool paused: false // clock A: enabled bound to false property bool shown: true // clock B: enabled bound to true property bool wanted: false // clock D: disabled from the start property int changesA: 0 property int changesB: 0 function out(key, value) { console.log("RESULT " + key + " " + JSON.stringify(value)) } function hms(d) { return Qt.formatDateTime(d, "HH:mm:ss") } SystemClock { id: clockA; precision: SystemClock.Seconds; enabled: root.paused; onDateChanged: root.changesA++ } SystemClock { id: clockB; precision: SystemClock.Seconds; enabled: root.shown; onDateChanged: root.changesB++ } SystemClock { id: clockD; precision: SystemClock.Seconds; enabled: root.wanted } Timer { interval: 2500 running: true onTriggered: { var a0 = root.changesA Wallclock.resync(clockA) root.out("A resync on enabled:false-bound clock", { enabled: clockA.enabled, dateChanged: root.changesA - a0 }) root.paused = true; root.out("A binding -> true", { enabled: clockA.enabled }) root.paused = false; root.out("A binding -> false", { enabled: clockA.enabled }) var b0 = root.changesB Wallclock.resync(clockB) root.out("B resync on enabled:true-bound clock", { enabled: clockB.enabled, dateChanged: root.changesB - b0 }) root.shown = false; root.out("B binding -> false", { enabled: clockB.enabled }) var whileDisabled = root.hms(clockD.date), now = root.hms(new Date()) root.wanted = true root.out("D disabled clock", { readWhileDisabled: whileDisabled, now: now, readAfterEnable: root.hms(clockD.date) }) Qt.quit() } } } QML QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen timeout 30 quickshell -p "$dir" --no-color 2>&1 | grep RESULT ``` At the PR head `4ca1505b0ccf999782f00a4b1ced68e107a63b90`: ``` DEBUG qml: RESULT A resync on enabled:false-bound clock {"enabled":false,"dateChanged":0} DEBUG qml: RESULT A binding -> true {"enabled":true} DEBUG qml: RESULT A binding -> false {"enabled":false} DEBUG qml: RESULT B resync on enabled:true-bound clock {"enabled":true,"dateChanged":1} DEBUG qml: RESULT B binding -> false {"enabled":true} DEBUG qml: RESULT D disabled clock {"readWhileDisabled":"04:38:51","now":"04:38:53","readAfterEnable":"04:38:53"} ``` At the previously reviewed head `51d42799e59e77e16143462555c8d59f00c987e0` (no early return): ``` DEBUG qml: RESULT A resync on enabled:false-bound clock {"enabled":true,"dateChanged":1} DEBUG qml: RESULT A binding -> true {"enabled":true} DEBUG qml: RESULT A binding -> false {"enabled":true} DEBUG qml: RESULT B resync on enabled:true-bound clock {"enabled":true,"dateChanged":1} DEBUG qml: RESULT B binding -> false {"enabled":true} DEBUG qml: RESULT D disabled clock {"readWhileDisabled":"04:38:54","now":"04:38:56","readAfterEnable":"04:38:56"} ``` Clock A (paused through a binding) is left alone at the head and keeps its binding; at the previous head the resync started it and dropped the binding. Clock B (bound `true`) is still resynced and still loses its binding at both heads, which the new docs text states. Clock D shows a disabled `SystemClock` reporting its construction time while disabled and re-reading the wall clock when enabled.

root\.lastTick\n)( root\.lastTick = now\n)/$2$1/' "$wc" mutate 'WallclockMath import removed' perl -ni -e 'print unless /^import "WallclockMath\.js" as Detect$/' "$wc" mutate 'jumped signal removed' perl -ni -e 'print unless /^ signal jumped\(real deltaMs\)$/' "$wc" } echo "clock-test.sh as in the PR:" run_all cat > "$tmp/extra.js" <<'JSX' // The emit itself, and what it needs: without these, a watchdog that never // raises `jumped` still passes every assertion above. assert(/^import "WallclockMath\.js" as Detect$/m.test(wallclockCode), 'Wallclock imports the tested predicate') assert(/^\s*signal jumped\(real deltaMs\)$/m.test(wallclockCode), 'Wallclock declares the signal the clocks listen for') assert(/var elapsed = now - root\.lastTick\s*\n\s*root\.lastTick = now\s*\n\s*if \(Detect\.isDiscontinuity\(elapsed, root\.interval, root\.threshold\)\) root\.jumped\(elapsed\)/.test(wallclockCode), 'each tick measures from the previous one and reports a step') JSX awk -v f="$tmp/extra.js" '$0 == "JS" { while ((getline l < f) > 0) print l } { print }' "$tmp/clock-test.sh.orig" > "$test" echo "clock-test.sh with the three assertions added:" run_all cp "$tmp/clock-test.sh.orig" "$test" ``` Output (Node v26.7.0, bash 5.3): ``` clock-test.sh as in the PR: unchanged exit=0 ok=175 jumped never emitted exit=0 ok=175 predicate negated exit=0 ok=175 baseline taken before subtracting exit=0 ok=175 WallclockMath import removed exit=0 ok=175 jumped signal removed exit=0 ok=175 clock-test.sh with the three assertions added: unchanged exit=0 ok=178 jumped never emitted exit=1 ok=175 predicate negated exit=1 ok=175 baseline taken before subtracting exit=1 ok=175 WallclockMath import removed exit=1 ok=173 jumped signal removed exit=1 ok=174 ```
